claims.text: failover.sh @ stage-4 runs on the host, needs no donhang-staging, applies echo-region.yaml to both regions with kubectl, then starts donhang-global-entry (caddy:2.10.0) on Docker network kind, publishing 127.0.0.1:18090 -> 8080, LB_POLICY passed as an environment variable.
claims.source_hint: scripts/k8s/failover.sh @ stage-4 lines 1-37

claims.text: global-entry.Caddyfile @ stage-4 lines 9-22: reverse_proxy donhang-north-control-plane:30090 then donhang-south-control-plane:30090; lb_policy {$LB_POLICY:first}; health_uri /; health_interval 2s; health_timeout 1s.
claims.source_hint: deploy/k8s/regions/global-entry.Caddyfile @ stage-4

claims.text: Caddy reverse_proxy lb_policy first chooses the first available upstream in the order they are defined; round_robin iterates each upstream in turn. Unhealthy upstreams are not available for selection.
claims.source_hint: Caddy 2.10 docs: Caddyfile directives > reverse_proxy > Load balancing (lb_policy first, round_robin)

claims.text: Setting health_uri enables Caddy's active health checks, run in the background on a timer every health_interval; no reply within health_timeout marks the upstream down; by default (health_fails 1, health_passes 1) one failed check marks it unhealthy and one passing check marks it healthy again.
claims.source_hint: Caddy 2.10 docs: reverse_proxy > Active health checks (health_uri, health_interval, health_timeout, health_status, health_passes, health_fails)

claims.text: In a Caddyfile, {$VAR:default} is replaced by the environment variable VAR when the Caddyfile is parsed (when Caddy loads it), or by default when VAR is not set.
claims.source_hint: Caddy 2.10 docs: Caddyfile Concepts > Environment variables

claims.text: Containers on a user-defined Docker network, such as kind's network kind, reach each other by container name through Docker's embedded DNS; kind names a cluster's node container <cluster>-control-plane and runs it on network kind.
claims.source_hint: Docker docs: Networking > Bridge network driver (user-defined bridges, DNS resolution between containers); kind docs: Known issues / design (network kind); Caddyfile comment lines 2-4

claims.text: docker pause suspends all processes in a container (on Linux through the freezer cgroup) and docker unpause resumes them.
claims.source_hint: Docker docs: CLI reference > docker container pause / unpause

claims.text: While north is paused, calls proxied to it hang or fail (curl gives up after 3 s); Caddy reverse_proxy does not retry another upstream by default, with first as with round_robin; new calls still go to north until an active health check fails, then every call goes to south.
claims.source_hint: Caddy 2.10 docs: reverse_proxy (Retries are disabled by default; dial_timeout); scripts/k8s/failover.sh lines 48-52; outputs/stage-4/scripts/k8s/failover.txt

claims.text: With lb_policy first, once the paused upstream passes a health check again it is first available, so the next calls go to north (failover.sh lines 64-69; output shows three north answers after unpause).
claims.source_hint: claims 3, 4; scripts/k8s/failover.sh lines 64-69; outputs/stage-4/scripts/k8s/failover.txt

claims.source_hint: scripts/k8s/failover.sh @ stage-4; scripts/lib/regions.sh line 7 (show prints then runs)

claims.source_hint: outputs/stage-4/scripts/k8s/failover.txt

claims.text: echo-region.yaml @ stage-4: Deployment echo-region (readiness probe GET / on 8080) answering only 'greetings from <node name>', keeping no state between calls, and a NodePort Service with nodePort 30090 in namespace regions, the same in every region.
claims.source_hint: deploy/gitops/config-repo/platform/regions/echo-region.yaml @ stage-4

claims.text: A NodePort Service opens its port on every node and forwards a connection there to a ready Pod selected by the Service; the readiness probe decides which Pods count as ready.
claims.source_hint: Kubernetes 1.34 docs: Service > type NodePort; Pod lifecycle > container probes (readiness)

claims.text: kind runs each cluster node as a Docker container; donhang-north and donhang-south are one-node clusters whose node containers are donhang-north-control-plane and donhang-south-control-plane.
claims.source_hint: kind docs: Quick Start / design; scripts/k8s/regions-up.sh @ stage-4

claims.text: With active checks only, the window in which Caddy still sends calls to an upstream that stopped answering is roughly one health_interval plus one health_timeout (about 3 s here); a longer interval widens it.
claims.source_hint: claim 4; Caddy 2.10 docs: reverse_proxy > Active health checks

claims.text: Opinion: when a recovered region may fail again, a team can make failing back a manual step so customers are not moved back and forth with each recovery; this Caddyfile cannot hold north back, so that needs a step outside it, e.g. restarting the entry with only south listed.
claims.source_hint: operational reasoning; outline item 5

claims.text: Opinion: in both active-passive and active-active, each region must be sized to carry the whole load when the other fails; active-active also requires every call to be servable by either region, which stateless Pods allow.
claims.source_hint: trade-off reasoning; k8s.l3.highly-available-entry-point summary line 5

claims.text: Opinion: active-passive leaves a fault that only the waiting region has undiscovered until failover; active-active exercises both regions every day.
claims.source_hint: trade-off reasoning

claims.text: Opinion: choose active-passive with manual failback when a region keeps failing and recovering; active-active when Pods keep no state and an idle region's cost dominates; active-passive when only one region may take writes.
claims.source_hint: trade-off reasoning; claims 16-18

claims.text: Opinion: the lab's single entry container is a single point of failure for both regions; a real setup can spread the entry over several sites, for example with DNS (not taught here).
claims.source_hint: outline item 6; k8s.l3.highly-available-entry-point
